_meta.description: Multi-turn cases. Each is a SEQUENCE of turns on one thread, testing that context carries across turns - pronoun resolution, 'tell me more', and topic switches.
_meta.why: Every other dataset here is single-turn, and single-turn evaluation cannot see the failure modes that memory introduces. A summarization change, a history-format change, or a query-expansion change can leave single-turn scores untouched while breaking every follow-up.
_meta.scoring: Assertions are per-turn and use the same fields as golden_qa.json. Turns with no assertions are setup only.
_meta.note: Keyword-based query expansion cannot resolve pronouns - 'tell me more about that one' expands to itself. These cases are therefore expected to lean on chat_history rather than retrieval, and are the strongest argument for testing retrieval.query_expansion.mode = 'llm'.

turns.question: Tell me more about the first one.
turns.notes: Pure pronoun resolution. Retrieval cannot help; this must come from chat_history.

turns.question: And what about your education?
turns.notes: A clean switch. The risk is the previous topic bleeding into the new answer.

turns.question: What was your most recent role?
And the others?
turns.notes: Two words, no nouns. Nothing but history can disambiguate this.

turns.question: Going back to the very first thing I asked - what were those skills again?
turns.notes: By this turn summarization has fired and the first exchange has been condensed. This is the case that catches a summarizer that drops content, and the reason the roll-forward fix in nodes/summarize.py matters.
